content.comment_body: Hello, I have a [company_name] BKS09-ATBM0520 absolute displacement sensor. I want to connect its data to my [product_name]. The sensor uses SSI signaling. Is it possible to connect this signal directly to [product_name]? If direct connection is not possible, is there a way to convert the SSI signal to Modbus so [product_name] can read it? Alternatively, is there a reasonably priced converter to change SSI to 4-20mA? Thank you!

Converting an SSI encoder signal to Modbus or 4-20mA may not be practical. The most affordable approach could be using a cord sensor with a potentiometer or 0-10V/4-20mA output. Could you describe your application and what resolution is required? Analog inputs have a range of 0 to 1000, roughly 10 bits. Regards, [user_name]

Thank you for your responses. I obtained two of these wire absolute sensors from work and plan to use one in my own application to detect four positions, similar to using "inductive sensors". I only need to know four piston positions with about +/- 1mm accuracy over a 0-1000mm range. My intention was to save costs by using the free sensor and to reduce work on mounting brackets and wiring that conventional inductive sensors would require.

It doesn't seem likely you'll save money with your existing sensors. Converter prices where you are may exceed €200 or $200. Perhaps consider converting your sensor with a multiturn potentiometer. Often, the mechanical system rotates 10-15 turns across the full measurement range, so replacing the sensor electronics with a 1kOhm multiturn potentiometer could be cost-effective, though more time-consuming. Regards, [user_name]
I've also found the cheapest converters are about €350. I'll likely proceed with the original plan using conventional inductive sensors.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users confirmed that [product_name] does not directly support SSI signals. Trying to convert SSI to compatible formats for [product_name] (such as 4-20mA or Modbus) was found to be costly, making it unfeasible in low-budget or DIY scenarios. The limited resolution of [product_name]'s analog input and lack of native support for SSI were key challenges to integration.
analysis.user_expectations: User wanted to connect or inexpensively convert the SSI signal from their sensor for use with [product_name], aiming for low cost and adequate accuracy. They hoped to utilize available equipment efficiently to save time and money.
